title: The Harbor Letter Archive
alt: Letters and archival documents arranged on a table
summary: A digital archive that organizes letters written by harbor workers between 1940 and 1960.
challenge: Hundreds of letters had inconsistent dates, names, and physical annotations, making them difficult for visitors to browse.
process: Mara created a small metadata vocabulary, grouped related correspondence, wrote image descriptions, and tested a chronological navigation structure.
outcome: The resulting prototype lets visitors move between people, years, and subjects while keeping each letter connected to its archival context.

title: Vanishing Storefronts
alt: Historic storefronts along a small town street
summary: A local-history project documenting small businesses that have disappeared from Port Alder.
challenge: The stories existed across family photographs, newspaper clippings, and personal memories without a shared structure.
process: Mara conducted short interviews, compared historic and present-day photographs, and organized each story around a place and its former community role.
outcome: The project presents concise histories that are easy to scan while preserving links to original sources and longer interview records.

title: Weather Room
alt: Archive materials related to a coastal storm
summary: An interactive story combining weather records, radio clips, maps, and fictional diary entries from a 1978 coastal storm.
focus: Narrative structure, audio, and archival media
challenge: Scientific records and personal stories used different timelines and levels of detail.
process: Mara aligned every source to a single storm timeline and designed short scenes that clearly distinguish historical records from fictional interpretation.
outcome: Visitors can follow the storm hour by hour, listen to selected clips, and inspect the sources behind each scene.

title: Tide Marks
alt: Diagram showing changes in coastal tide levels
summary: A simple digital visualization of fifty years of tide records and shoreline change.
challenge: A large table of measurements made long-term patterns difficult for a general audience to understand.
process: Mara cleaned the records, selected representative intervals, and paired each visual pattern with a plain-language explanation.
outcome: The final concept communicates long-term change without hiding uncertainty or requiring visitors to understand technical datasets.
